items.text: No single mask breaks you. Masking debt is the interest — years of overriding your real responses to fit a world that wasn't built for you. People who "seemed fine for decades" aren't suddenly fragile. The bill just came due.
items.rationale: Turns the 'debt' metaphor from the briefing into a quotable reframe that explains the late-onset burnout collapse without pathologizing. Identity-neutral, no advice, high recognition for late-diagnosed adults.

items.text: For a lot of ADHDers, bracing for rejection hurts worse than the rejection itself. You flinch harder than the moment actually lands. Being told you're "oversensitive" just deepens it. That's a sensitization pattern, not drama.
items.rationale: Names the precise anticipation>event mechanism from the 2026 RSD study. Kept experiential to avoid clinical overreach; counters the 'oversensitive' shame the study itself flags.
items.sensitivity_flag: Describes an emotional pattern, not a diagnosis or treatment — kept first-person/experiential to stay clear of medical-claim territory; confident it's within the rules.

items.text: What if "poor social skills" was never the whole story? The communication gap between autistic and non-autistic people runs both ways — and autistic people often connect easily with each other. So who's really missing whom?
items.rationale: Poses the double empathy problem as genuine inquiry, matching the live Milton/Fellowes debate. 'Often' hedges the autistic-autistic claim per the source; opens conversation rather than baiting.
